newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 28.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The City of London police has warned financial institutions that millions of dollars of stolen American bonds have started to appear in London and other European capitals. The bonds were stolen by the Mafia from a wastepaper recycling company in New Jersey ten years ago.
BACKING FOR SHELL IN FIGHT AGAINST REBELS

The Association of British Insurers is backing Royal Dutch/Shell at its forthcoming AGM over a resolution calling for the company to adopt a tighter line on the environment and its business ethics. The resolution is backed by Pirc and a number of pension funds and religious institutions.

Motor manufacturer Lotus, which is owned by Malaysia's Proton, is to invest 60 million stg on a new development over the next two years. It will take on more than 300 engineers and produce a range of new cars.
G7'S INACTION SPARKS A FRESH DOLLAR GAIN

The Group of Seven industrial nations failed to take action over the rising value of the dollar at this weekend's meeting. However, they promised to monitor developments and co-operate with appropriate markets.
